$comment: Numbers that BOTH the Python ingest pipeline and the TypeScript viewer have to agree on.
This file exists because they did not. `pipeline/views.py` used 6.0 mm and
`src/viewer/beamDim.ts` used 5 mm for the same physical quantity — the elevation
half-thickness of the slab a sector is treated as imaging — so the sweep scrubber
would have named structures the on-screen highlight did not mark, and neither number
was wrong on its own face. A constant duplicated across two languages is a constant
that will drift, and this one drifts invisibly: both values render something plausible.
Python reads it with json.load; TypeScript imports it directly, and Vite inlines it at
build time, so there is no runtime fetch. tests/unit/beamDim.test.ts pins the TS
constant against this file.
Add a number here only when two languages genuinely both need it. This is not a
settings file, and it is not the content pack — anything a VIEW owns belongs in
pack.json, where it can be authored and reviewed per view.
Half-thickness of the slab about the imaging plane that a sector is treated as
imaging. An echo plane is not a mathematical plane: a sector is an elevation-focused
slice several millimetres thick, and on a paediatric phased array that is roughly
3-6 mm at the focus and worse away from it.
6.0 won over the viewer's 5, for two reasons that point the same way.
First, the three shipped views were authored and validated against 6.0 —
`Sector.contains` and `require_in_plane` both use it as the tolerance a landmark has
to fall within. Adopting 5 would silently re-derive content: the views would be
re-checked against a tighter rule they were never placed to satisfy, and a view that
failed would be a pipeline error rather than a considered decision.
Second, the two uses fail in opposite directions and 6 is the safe end of both. In the
pipeline it is a TOLERANCE on whether a landmark is close enough to the plane, where
being generous risks accepting a slightly off view and being strict risks refusing a
correct one for a millimetre. In the viewer it is the thickness of a HIGHLIGHT, where
one extra millimetre is imperceptible. So the value is set by the use that can
actually be wrong.
